the monodromies of the fundamental solutions to associated linear systems of the null-cur- vature equations are universal invariants of their solutions and can be used to parameterize the spaces of local solu- tions of the null-curvatures equations and their reductions.

the spaces of solutions to the null-curvature system are the spaces of holomorphic functions in the spectral plane with the prescribed monodromy, and the monodromies of solutions of the null-curvatures equations are determined by the Jordan forms of the corresponding matrices.

the spaces of local (i.e., defined on a domain in a plane with a finite number of points deleted) solutions of integrable reduction of Einstein’s field equation can be parameterized in terms of the monodronomy data of associated linear systems and that the inverse problem of finding the local solutions for given monodromy can be solved unamiguously.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: given an integrable reduction of Einstein’s field equation, to determine the monodromic properties of its local solution spaces, i.e., to determine which monodromy problems can be solved univocally.

the monodromic aspects of the integrable reductions of the Einstein’s field equations, which can be considered as a generalization of the classical monodromy problem of the theory of linear ordinary differential equations.
the monodromic aspects of the spaces of solutions to the integrable reductions of the Einstein field equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the monodromic properties of the fundamental solutions are the most essential feature of the integrable systems of partial differential equations, which can be considered as the most important characteristic of integrability.

the monodromic approach to the integrable reductions of the Einstein field equations is the most effective and universal method for solving the problem of constructing the spaces of local exact solutions of Einstein’s equations.
the monodromies of the fundamental solutions to the linear systems associated with the integrable reductions of the Einstein equations are the universal parameters of the spaces of solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “monodromic” parameterization of the spaces of solutions to the integrable reductions of the Einstein equations provides a new approach to the problem of the global description of these spaces.

we have found the complete set of the necessary and sufficient conditions for the local existence of a solution of the null curvature equations for the Jordan forms of the desired variables and also have found the explicit forms of all such solutions.

the spaces of local integrable solutions of various reductions of Einstein’s equations are parameterized in a universal manner, i.e., in the form of the monodronmy data of the associated linear problems, which are independent of the specific equations under consideration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a wide class of integrable reductions, the spaces of solutions are parameterized by the monodromies, which are universal (i.e. independent of the particular solutions) and can be computed by solving linear algebraic problems.

, at least in the case of two-dimensional fields, the monodromic data of the corresponding linear systems can serve as a universal parameterization of the spaces of solutions to integrable reductions of the Einstein equations.
